html:
SMTO-SKL-0154 — SMTO doesn't know which GitHub account to use

GUID: 1f3dff9e-1772-5137-8546-f790b59ec5e6
Slug: github-account-ambiguous
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • More than one GitHub account is saved in SMTO and this request didn't say which one to use. SMTO won't guess, so nothing was sent to GitHub.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to list your GitHub accounts, and note the name of the one you want to use. This shows every saved account SMTO could choose from.
  2. Repeat your request and pick that account: type @ in the message box and choose the GitHub account entry from Parameter Store, or name the account in your message. Once one account is named, SMTO no longer has to choose between them.
  3. If you no longer use one of the accounts, open Parameter Store, select that entry and choose Delete parameter. Only do this if you are sure you don't need it. With a single saved account, SMTO uses it automatically for future requests.

What success looks like

  • SMTO answers your GitHub request and shows the account it used.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste a GitHub token into the chat to pick an account.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub account selection found more than one eligible github_account profile and no explicit account_ref or uniquely accepted parameter binding.

What this means

  • Account selection has more than one candidate and no unique explicit or accepted account identity. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Account selection has more than one candidate and no unique explicit or accepted account identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe github.accounts results and accepted bindings.

How to fix it

  • GitHubProfiles.account raises account_ambiguous when no account_ref is supplied and the accepted bindings (or, without bindings, all github_account records) contain more than one profile; details.account_refs lists the candidates. Call github.accounts and pass the exact account_ref, or bind exactly one GitHub Account parameter in the conversation; never select by list order or by broader permissions.
  • Use github.accounts and supply the exact account_ref. Do not select the first account or a broader token.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • One intended account_ref is selected without choosing by broader permission or list order.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
